state.declaration: I keep my palm flat on the rack and let it walk the whole of the borrowed stock, one piece at a time, until the stallkeeper has named each one's purpose, its price, and the work it was taken out for — no hurry, no haggling, just the naming. Then I take exactly one down off the pegs: the piece that answers the lamp burning wrong in that corridor, the piece a body could carry and still sleep beside on hard ground after a long inland march. I set it on the board between us with the clasp open and the maker's mark turned up, make him speak the full price aloud before a single coin leaves my pouch, and then I lay the coin down flat and close the clasp with my own hand. Whatever he thinks of the choice is his business; the tool comes with me, and tomorrow it earns its keep.
